codeReview.summary: The commit correctly adds canonical comparators and restores {corpus} placeholders for cli-stream scenarios, but it does not preserve stdin-driven stream behavior as required by the feature description.

issues.description: `_scenario()` now always emits `{pattern} {corpus}` even when `stdin_data` is present. Stream scenarios therefore render commands like `ag ... {pattern} .` (see manifests/scenarios.json:207-247). The parity runner still pipes `stdin_data` but also executes the expanded file argument (`cmd_template.replace(...).replace('{corpus}', corpus)` in scripts/parity/run_matrix.py:287-300), which defeats the intended stdin-only stream path described there (scripts/parity/run_matrix.py:283-285). This violates the feature requirement to preserve stdin-driven stream behavior.

sharedStateObservations.observation: benchmark-worker emphasizes comparator completeness but does not explicitly guard stdin/stream semantics when enforcing manifest-template integrity, which allowed a change that satisfies placeholder/comparator checks while regressing stream execution semantics.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/skills/benchmark-worker/SKILL.md:18-20 focuses on comparator completeness; .factory/library/user-testing.md:26-27 states cli-count-stream must cover stdin/stream behavior and that stream checks depend on stream-mode flag semantics.

summary: Fail: comparator-completeness and corpus-placeholder integrity were fixed, but the implementation no longer preserves stdin-driven stream behavior for cli-stream scenarios because stream commands now include an expanded corpus argument during execution.
